summary: rustre-debug-macos is a platform-specific debugger backend (Mach ports). The MCP server (rustre-mcp) does not depend on or expose any tool from rustre-debug-macos, so no JSON-RPC tool calls exist that surface this crate's behaviour. Comparison performed instead by (a) running the standalone Python validator (pure-data re-implementation) and (b) source-inspecting the Rust crate to confirm every constant / mapping in the validator matches the canonical Rust definitions.

tests.name: validator_self_test
tests.method: python validator built-in asserts (BreakpointManager, x86_64/arm64 register indices, CpuType, MachoFileType)
tests.mcp_result: n/a (no MCP tool exposes this crate)

tests.name: x86_64_register_index_table
tests.method: compare Python _X86_64 dict vs Rust MacosRegisterSet::x86_64_index match arms (lib.rs:96-119)

tests.name: arm64_register_index_table
tests.method: compare Python arm64_index() vs Rust MacosRegisterSet::arm64_index (lib.rs:123-136); x0-x28 -> 0..28, fp/x29 -> 29, lr/x30 -> 30, sp -> 31, pc -> 32, cpsr -> 33

tests.name: macho_magic_constants
tests.method: Python macho_magic vs Rust pub mod macho_magic (lib.rs:1424-1437)

tests.name: MacosDebugger_identity
tests.method: Python MacosDebugger.NAME / SUPPORTED_ARCHS vs Rust name()/supported_architectures()

notes: Crate is target_os=macos gated. On Windows host the non-macOS stub Debugger impl returns DebugError::Unsupported for all calls; only the pure-data structures (BreakpointManager, MacosRegisterSet, macho_magic, CpuType, MachoFileType, MacosDebugger name/archs) are exercisable and match the validator exactly. No MCP-server JSON-RPC tool currently wraps this crate, so no live stdio test was applicable.
